mode: Office environment refinement: Primer-inspired Copilot studio
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized game environment and ui-mockup.
Create a creative OFFICE-ENVIRONMENT refinement of image 1. The user likes the direction but now wants the OFFICE ITSELF to carry more GitHub Primer Brand personality. Produce one polished landscape 16:9 in-game mock-up, sharp and readable. The architecture, furnishings and spatial composition must change meaningfully; this is not just another button recolor.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the selected Codex interface and current scene to edit. Preserve its functional content, selected character and quiet Primer Brand UI vocabulary.
Image 2 is the actual Hub world reference: matte low-poly geometry, small scale campus architecture, faceted trees, calm daylight, floating digital space.
Image 3 is the actual exterior Lab asset: off-white horizontal slabs, blue-gray frames, simple modular construction. Extend this material family into a plausible proposed interior.
Image 4 is the canonical orange Developer head; preserve its identity and geometry.

CREATIVE DIRECTION — THE COPILOT STUDIO:
Reimagine this as a compact, beautifully composed creative studio / Tower observatory inside the central Lab. Make Primer's rounded-rectangle shapes, controlled display colors, light/dark layering and spacious typography architectural. The space should feel friendly, collectible and unmistakably part of a low-poly game.
Pull the camera back modestly and lift it slightly, giving a gentle three-quarter sense of the room and enough space to see its surrounding architecture, a little floor, a side bench and a sculptural overhead frame. Keep the controls nearly frontal and text legible. The live character and its controls remain the main focal point; not a distant tiny screen.

ARCHITECTURE:
Build one broad, off-white squared arch / rounded-rectangle portal around the Codex station, shaped from thick, simple low-poly slabs with small planar bevels. Its inner reveal is deep indigo with one restrained pale-teal light seam. This arch connects a modest ceiling canopy to the desk and creates an intentional alcove, not a giant sci-fi tunnel.
Replace the plain blue-gray office wall area with a considered arrangement of ivory wall planes, one deep-indigo inset, and a short run of lavender-to-indigo vertical acoustic fins on one side. Use only a few large clean shapes and clear material boundaries. The palette is light stone #e8ecf2, dark ink/navy, pale indigo #b1b9fb, indigo #7a82f0, and small teal #89ebe1/#22d3c7 accents. These are color guidance, never printed codes.
Keep a wide corner window with slim blue-gray mullions framing recognizable campus pathways, teal faceted trees and benches. It still clearly belongs to the Hub. Do not show a duplicate Lab outside.
Introduce one simple built-in window bench with muted lavender cushions, a small matching geometric planter with a canonical low-poly teal tree, and a short shelf with two or three plain solid-color books. These are supporting office details, not a cluttered lounge. A small abstract branch-and-node wall light, made from one thin line and three dots, can provide a subtle software-themed identity. No slogans or extra branding text.

THE STATION BECOMES PART OF THE ROOM:
Replace the feeling of two enormous monitors sitting on a generic desk with a continuous purpose-designed station. Left collection is a recessed vertical wall rack in the same ivory frame. The center is an OPEN three-dimensional display alcove with the actual floating Developer on a low faceted plinth. Its indigo backdrop is part of the room, not a computer screen containing a flat character illustration. Stats sit on one slim dark panel built into the alcove's right side. A clean cantilevered ivory desk/sill joins all three sections; dark-blue undercut and a very subtle teal underside line give it a light floating feel. Keep a believable support or wall mounting.
Integrate the animation row into the front sill in a recessed indigo console. No chunky keyboard, no giant beveled tablet frame. Smooth simple rounded-rectangle controls have one slim lower lip and short contact shadows, so they remain tactile.
A small portion of the floor should be visible: large quiet pale-gray slabs with a deep-indigo geometric inset and one restrained curved teal seam echoing the Hub's digital currents. This is floor design, not a giant circuit-board pattern.
The workstation should feel like architecture and furniture designed together, with a slightly playful sculptural quality.

PRESERVE THE APPROVED INTERFACE:
Header COPILOT / TOWER DEFENSE and "Copilot Hub / Tower Codex", set quietly on the architecture or as a clean game HUD. Maintain the existing game identity. No added GitHub logo, Octocat, fictitious corporate slogan or code blocks.
Clear "Back to Hub" in the upper right.
Left seven portrait plaques preserve the arrangement, canonical portrait colors and these exact names: "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter". Developer selected with pale-indigo edge and small check marker. Existing unavailable models remain quiet silhouettes. No extra Towers or duplicate cards.
Main title "Developer", subtitle "Direct-output specialist". Clear Mona Sans-style hierarchy, generous spacing, sentence case.
Stats at right: "Stats", "Damage", "Work", "Action speed", "Range", "Compute". Small consistent Octicon-like glyphs: zap, code, meter, crosshairs, cpu. Segmented visual gauges only: damage below halfway, work full, action speed full, range about two-thirds, compute mostly filled. Quiet indigo filled cells, teal only for Compute. ABSOLUTELY NO stat numbers, digits, units, percentages, prices, totals or rankings.
Exactly SEVEN animation choices in a single row: "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve". Idle alone selected pale indigo with dark label and check. No extra blank key. Small leading icons. Label "Animations".
Animation selection only. NO speed controls, play/pause transport, scrubber, timeline, replay button or loop toggle.
Keep camera rotation arrows, camera "Reset", and "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom". Camera controls remain visually separate from animation choices.

MODEL AND RENDERING:
The Developer is a hovering HEAD ONLY, faceted orange swept hair/spikes, dark angular goggles with teal lenses, black face with exactly two cyan eye strokes, cream ear pieces with curly-brace glyph. No body, new accessories, recoloring or redesign. Render it physically in the alcove with honest contact shadow below.
Use the game's stylized low-poly rendering throughout, flat matte colors, broad soft daylight, gentle ambient occlusion and clean faceted geometry. Simple bevels rather than glossy curves. Slight local indigo/teal lighting is allowed in the alcove, but no overall neon nightclub, cyberpunk machinery, photoreal material grain, heavy bloom, cinematic blur or dramatic spotlights.
The result must show a notably more distinctive Primer-inspired office while preserving the warm, quiet Hub world and an operable game interface. No external presentation labels, comparison frames, browser chrome or concept-board callouts.
